skill.name: accessibility-fundamentals
skill.description: Reviews React and JSX interfaces for accessibility basics, including semantic elements, labels, keyboard access, focus visibility, ARIA use, and practical WCAG checks.
skill.summary: Guides accessible React and JSX reviews for forms, buttons, navigation, modals, and other interactive UI.
skill.author: DanielPodolsky

security_audit.summary: All external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and fenced JSX, CSS, testing, and MCP examples in SKILL.md. The system reconnaissance finding is also a false positive for a CSS focus outline declaration. No prompt injection, credential handling, exfiltration intent, or malicious behavior was found.

static_findings.snippet: - [ ] **Form labels** — Every input has an associated `<label>`
- [ ] **Remove focus outlines** — Never `outline: none` without replacement
- [ ] **Use divs for buttons** — Use semantic `<button>` or `<a>`
**Why it matters:** `<div onClick>` doesn't receive keyboard focus, doesn't respond to Enter/Space,
| `aria-labelledby` | Points to element with visible label |
| `aria-hidden="true"` | Hides decorative icons from screen readers |
| `<div onClick>` | "What happens when a keyboard user tries to click this?" |
| `outline: none` | "How does a keyboard user know where they are?" |
| `tabIndex > 0` | "This breaks natural tab order. Why is it needed?" |

content.value_statement: Interactive React interfaces often miss keyboard, labeling, and focus requirements. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical WCAG checks for JSX, forms, navigation, and dialogs.
actual_capabilities: Checks interactive JSX for semantic buttons, links, headings, and form controls.
Flags missing labels, weak link text, icon-only buttons, and inaccessible placeholders.
Reviews keyboard access, visible focus states, modal escape paths, and focus trapping needs.
Explains practical ARIA patterns such as aria-label, aria-describedby, aria-live, and aria-expanded.
Suggests manual checks for keyboard navigation, zoom behavior, screen readers, and automated axe testing.
limitations: It does not run automated accessibility tests by itself.
It is not a full WCAG certification or legal compliance audit.
It focuses on React and JSX patterns more than native mobile or desktop interfaces.
Screen reader behavior, contrast ratios, and complex focus flows still require human verification.

use_cases.title: Review a React form before merge
use_cases.description: Check labels, error messages, invalid states, and keyboard behavior before a pull request is approved.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a design system component
use_cases.description: Assess buttons, icon controls, modals, menus, and navigation patterns for reusable accessibility issues.

use_cases.title: Prepare interview-ready accessibility notes
use_cases.description: Turn implementation work into clear examples about semantic HTML, focus management, and inclusive design decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner JSX Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when reviewing a small component with buttons, links, or inputs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this JSX for basic accessibility. Focus on semantic elements, labels, alt text, keyboard access, and visible focus states.

prompt_templates.title: Form Accessibility Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when reviewing a form with validation or dynamic error messages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this form for accessibility. Check label associations, error message linking, aria-invalid use, placeholder dependence, and keyboard completion.

prompt_templates.title: Interactive Component Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when reviewing modals, menus, accordions, or custom controls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this interactive component for keyboard behavior, focus management, escape paths, accessible names, and appropriate ARIA state.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Release Gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before shipping a complex React interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release-ready accessibility review. Prioritize WCAG impact, user risk, manual test coverage, automated test gaps, and concrete remediation steps.

output_examples.input: A pull request adds an icon-only delete button and a form with placeholder-only fields.
output_examples.output: The review identifies missing accessible names and missing form labels, explains the user impact, and recommends visible labels plus a clear button name.

output_examples.input: A modal component opens from a navigation menu and closes only through a mouse click.
output_examples.output: The review highlights missing keyboard escape behavior, focus trapping requirements, and the need to return focus to the trigger.

output_examples.input: A page uses colored status badges and removes default focus outlines.
output_examples.output: The review flags color-only meaning and invisible keyboard focus, then suggests text indicators and a visible focus style.

best_practices: Start with semantic HTML before adding ARIA attributes.
Test every interactive flow with a keyboard before approving changes.
Pair automated axe checks with manual screen reader, zoom, and focus review.
anti_patterns: Using div or span elements as buttons without native keyboard behavior.
Using placeholders as the only label for form fields.
Removing focus outlines without a visible replacement.

faq.question: Does this skill run accessibility tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and test suggestions, but the user or agent must run the actual tools.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it fit best?
faq.answer: It fits React and JSX best, especially components with forms, buttons, navigation, dialogs, and custom interactions.

faq.question: Does it replace a WCAG audit?
faq.answer: No. It helps find common issues, but formal compliance requires broader testing and expert review.

faq.question: Can it help with ARIA decisions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains common ARIA attributes and encourages semantic HTML before adding ARIA.

faq.question: What should I provide for the best review?
faq.answer: Provide the component code, expected user flow, validation behavior, and any design requirements for focus or state.

faq.question: Is it useful for designers?
faq.answer: Yes. Designers can use it to check labels, focus states, color dependence, and interaction requirements before handoff.
